title: How do I open my game up as a beta?
author: NinjaLegacyDev
selftext:
For the last few weeks I’ve been designing a game and having Claude 5.5 build it piece by piece. I’m on Version 91 now.

I’m getting to the point where I would like other players to be able to play it in its beta form as I continue adding and changing things to make it a better experience but the game has leaderboards, guilds, and other shared systems between players. 

Is there a free way that I can put my game out there where I can keep updating it and the players levels, leaderboards, and such won’t be affected after I roll out updates?

(Context: The game is built using html and what Claud says is “.js” files I think? I have no experience in game development which is why I took this route. I also want to make sure that someone can’t just swipe up my code and go publish it themselves.)

comments.author: NinjaLegacyDev
comments.body: I don’t have a Steam page yet. Does that cost money?

replies.author: Shalke97
replies.body: Yes, it costs 100 Euros to set up a product on Steam. It's a tedious step and also requires tax information. But thats the first real step into Game Development.

comments.author: metruzanca
comments.body: Yeah, that's a web game. So you should accept people can steal that and just not worry about it.

replies.author: NinjaLegacyDev
replies.body: Okay thanks! Do you know how I should go about getting it on the web where it’s “multiplayer-lite” where their leaderboards and stuff aren’t just saved in their system and it’s in a server? I’ve heard about a few different ways but it seems complicated.

replies.author: metruzanca
replies.body:
There are so many different ways.

Personally, I use Railway. It's very AI friendly with their MCP and it's also very beginner-friendly.

Then just ask your AI to build you a simple backend leaderboard that connects with your web game and have it publish it on railway.

(that being said leaderboards are fairly easy to cheat unless you spend a lot of time in figuring out how to prevent that from happening. But as a first proof of concept and way to get people playing the game, it'll be fine.)

replies.author: NinjaLegacyDev
replies.body: Chatgpt told me to use another system that would basically keep account info, leaderboards, stats, etc so that if a player changes their games numbers it wouldn’t actually affect the back end numbers, it would be strictly visual to them. Do you think this could be an option too? This game is like a mmo-lite/rpg and I want it to be as clean as possible

replies.author: metruzanca
replies.body: Nothing is going to stop a player from reverse engineering your API calls and send whatever stats they want. Again, I would not waste a lot of time on this, ship your game, and worry about it later. Just be aware that this is possible.

replies.author: metruzanca
replies.body: I would also not use Chat GPT for architectural planning, use a coding agent like Claude. The models used in Chat GPT are fairly dumb usually as they're optimized for human conversation, not building things.
